I must say it was a great frustration for us...

Great if there is a long line and terrific if your wanting detailed history of specific things. The quide is everything and what they are passionate about. Down side is you are rushed through and can miss a lot. Overall lest with more than I would have on our own.

We had an excellent tour with Alex. He is extremely knowledgeable, helpful and interactive guide who made our 3 hours at the Louvre fly by. He not only provide a historical background to the major pieces we saw but also answered related questions asked by tour attendees. He didn't simply drone on but provide humor, perspective and solicited interaction with the tour group. The Louvre itself is amazing as everyone knows. We would have easily spent 1/2-1 hour trying to find our way around the Louvre, so a guided tour made the most of our time.

The Louvre was spectacular. Our guide, Valerie, mentioned that it would take 4 months to go through the entire thing. It was the perfect amount. Glad we got to see Mona Lisa even though they moved her. Valerie has very engaging stories and kept everyone very interested the whole time (hard to do with a big group!). It was so cute to watch her light up when she spoke of the uniqueness and the stories of each thing. Even though she sees it a lot, she made the museum come alive for us. Great tour! Much better than just doing audio by yourself.

This was an excellent tour!! Alex was our guide and was really wonderful. He was knowledgeable and also had a sense of humor! Worth every penny for skip the line and an organized efficient way to see the highlights of the Louvre.

Without this consice tour it is impossible for a novice couple like us to even figure out the ocean of Louvre.. language being a major problem for English speaking people , as the subtitle description s are also only in French. Our guide was quick and right up to the mark , still was tiring in 3 hours to get a around idea of the vast meusium..

Took the Versailles tour to take advantage of the coach ride to the castle and the skip the line ticket. the bus was comfortable and on time and the skip the line tickets saved us standing in heat waiting access.
the guide Inna was very informative and liked to give little tidbits of information as the tour progressed the headsets were good to have once we figured out batteries had to be changed on Inna's set since we all were getting same static. however once online the headsets were handy in the crowds in case we got separated but we could still hear comments even if we were stuck in back

can't control crowds so guide made efforts to stop and gather us up every so often to point out special items -

The one most important place to visit on your trip to Paris is the Lourve! It is highly recommended that you purchase your access with tour guide in the appropriate language prior to your visit. The waiting line just for tickets at the Louvre can be quite long and without a guide who can provide the understanding of many of the pieces to be seen, you are adrift as a block of wood in a storm. Our English speaking guide had an excellent knowledge of history and the many cultures that merged to create "Western" views of art, science and religion and his comments truly helped those of us in his tour group to appreciate the many items we were seeing as we traveled through the galleries of the museum. We got our access via TripAdvisor about 45 days prior to our trip to Paris. The cost of the access with the guide is a bargain!!!

Although the Louvre is always packed, we loved this tour. Our tour guide Anna was wonderful. We enjoyed everything about the tour. We did have to wait in a very long line to see Mona Lisa, however Anna kept us entertained with her knowledge the entire tour. It’s a beautiful museum. However you would need weeks to see it all, she took us to all the important sights and answered any and all questions. Make sure you look map over, so at the end you can see the things other than on tour. Anna was available to. Help guide you to other areas. It’s a good way to get introduced to the Louvre:

Our tour code was Rueben. Very nice and very knowledgeable. He told us great stories about selected artworks and timed the tour to go when the Mona Lisa’s was least crowded. He was genuinely concerned to make our visit memorable. Best tour guide we’ve ever had!
I came with my wife and daughter & son-in-law. Well worth the visit. Artwork was amazing! Worth the trip to see the Mona Lisa.
Our Tour guide Reuben was great! We got to see everything we wanted to including the Mona Lisa! Don’t know how you would get through and see everything without a knowledgeable guide!

This tour was Fabulous- largely because of our tour guide Fabrizia - ‘Fab’ for short-and she was fab!! Fabulous to be exact. Fab’s passion for art history came through as she effortlessly guided us through the Louvre, introducing us to her favourite pieces and sharing the history of the times with us. It was a lovely way to experience this vast museum and again, if you have a chance to request Fab as your tour guide, do so!!! She made the tour very memorable- thank you Fab!!
Nancy, Alan and Soph 😊

Zdravko or “Z” as he likes to be called is a spectacular guide. He kept a group of 26 of us moving smoothly through the museum, and was a wealth of knowledge. We benefited tremendously from Z’s experience as an art History Major and his English is was spot on. This tour was the highlight of our trip.

Other was unforgettable experience. Of course it's one of the most famous landmarks in the world. THE LOUVRE.
We had an outstanding guide ALEX and he maid our visit unforgettable.
VERY knolegible, but also funny and caring, he gave us outstanding tour of history, art, French hospitality.
It's definitely the tour to take.
The tour was excellent and we enjoyed the tour guide - the art selected was perfect. If you have limited time at the Louvre - skip the Mona Lisa!

She taught us so many new things to notice when looking at the art. Our only issue was equipment- the little radios we were given to listen to her talk on cut in and out a bit and while she did her best to fix the equipment, it was a problem for most of us on the tour. But, it was only a small issue and we were able to hear 95% of the tour. Very awesome tour!! Wish we had thought to get more pictures!!
We had a great time touring Louvre with Ruben (not sure about the spelling of his name). This tour is manageable for families with younger children using a stroller.

If it is your first time in the Louvre, a guide is a must. The place is expansive and is overwhelming. Our guide was a expert on both the museum and the art. Well worth the money. Skipping the line is also a must. Go early!

We saw all the important pieces, including Mona Lisa, which with her security is a trip unto itself. Claire had my attention and really helped me to block out all the other people there with other guides and on their own. I'd highly suggest to anyone that they have a guided tour with the Louvre. Otherwise it's totally overwhelming and way too much to do on your own without a solid plan. Claire really cared about us and loves France and the Louvre. She shared insights into the artists as her art history background added to her stories. A wonderful way to spend a morning.

We had an excellent tour guide that handled the group very well and answered all the questions. It was a fun informative way to see the Louvre Museum that can be quite overwhelming if you try and do it by yourself.
As you have seen, this is a must if not the #1 site to visit. Give it some time so you can appreciate the history

Wow- what an amazing place. We loved everything about the Louvre inside and out. Our guide was great. She was very knowledgeable and had a fun personality. She made sure everyone was comfortable. Highly recommend the tour. After the tour you can visit extra parts of the Lourve on your own. It’s s full day so wear comfortable shoes and make sure you make an effort to have a coffee or wine on the balcony. We Love Paris and would go back again and again.

Booked the skip the line Louve tour and the company who ran the tour City Wonders done a great job.
Groups were split up with different tour guides and we were so lucky that we got Alex as our tour guide.
The metting point is very easy to find for First time visitors to Paris.
Entry was fast and after seeing the long queues it was a very wise choice to book this tour.
Alex changed plans on the go so we visited Mona Lisa first to avoid the massive queue later in the morning.
He show us the main attractions in the Louve and explained the story and History behind them and if you done this by yourself you would more than likely just walk past.
Book this tour with confidence and hope you get Alex.

Lo was our guide today. Our tour started started from from ancient times and worked its way up through the centuries. It was well planned out and Lo got my teenager actively involved with the art. Lo was friendly and you could tell she loved her job. Her enthusiasm pulled us right in. There was never a dull moment. Great way to be introduced to the Louvre.

We were amazed at the items we saw inside the Louvre. The Mona Lisa is the tip of the iceberg when you walk through all the rooms. One in particular was the Napolean apartment, and there was of course, Venus de Milo, Like most places people visiit, you do have to put up with the visitors who think nothing of walking through your picture taking or just barging in front of you.
I know Louvre is really big and you cannot see everything on one day, but the tour really showed the 3 most important things. tour guide was nice and could tell a lot, but there was no time.

Do not try to see the Louvre on your own unless you plan to spend days there. Even with a guide, you will only see a small portion. But, you will hit key areas and get an education in the process. Worth every penny.

I have visited Paris many times and have never been to the Louvre because I felt overwhelmed by it.
Purchasing this tour was my best decision.
I thoroughly enjoyed the museum and the tour. My tour guide, Felix, was wonderful! He was entertaining, friendly and extremely knowledgeable.
He made my trip to the Louvre an amazing experience. Thank you !

Great tour. Very informative & interesting even for those not in to art. Our guide was amazing. Former teacher, from Paris, very knowledgeable and funny!
3 hours of walking and standing so very hard in old legs.
WOW is one word that can describe this amazing place. Get a guided tour is faster and you will learn a lot about this amazing place.

Our tour guide Alistair (or was his name Hogan?) was fantastic! He was very knowledgeable and had a great personality. Having been born and raised in Paris allowed him to provide extra snippets that we otherwise wouldn’t have known about the history. He made the tour interesting and kept us thoroughly engaged. Definitely glad I went!
Great tour to both skip the crazy lines and see all the key highlights in just 3 hours! The guide was very knowledgeable and informative.
Great tour, maybe suggest somewhere on booking page about tour duration. We were not expecting 3 hours.

We had the good fortune to be placed on "Team Adam" for this tour. The tour guide Adam was absolutely the best guide - funny, entertaining, understandable, and extremely knowledgeable. I have two children so I knew I couldn't spend all day in the Louvre. They didn't want to go at all, but I wanted them to at least get the highlights. In two hours, Adam was able to show us the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, the famous Winged Victory statue, and a few more important pieces and explain them in way that we could all appreciate them. Imagine my surprise when my kids, who didn't want to go to the Louvre, told me at the end of our Paris vacation that our Louvre tour was their absolutely favorite thing we did all week! Honestly, Adam was amazing - this tour is definitely worth it!

No waiting for tickets or entrance, brief security line and Alistair was kind, funny and made sure group remained together. If you want a hassle-free Louvre experience where your guide gets you to Mona Lisa and other highlights without you having to figure things out yourself and adds great stories- then book this. Was just right for my teenagers and I.

To no fault of our tour guide Who was awesome the tour company was a total mess!!! When we checked in at the meeting place there where not tickets for us!!! It timed then one hour to work this out and we go to do the tour late. I front of us there was another family that we as ben waiting since 11AM ( our tour was at 2:30) and they hand not tickets! I think if not for our tour guide we also would have been left out!!! If you are doing this the private tour is the way to go! The other tours have way to many people!!! This is a massive place and a lot can get lost in such a large group! I can not give it a higher score because of the ticket mess!

Normal entry tickets to le Louvre were booked out so this was the only way to get into the museum within our schedule. We booked the 9.00am start which meant that we could stay on after the tour for the rest of the day. A bit more expensive but entry took less that 20minutes.
The tour itself was more of a quick orientation of the building and visited the busy attractions. The English speaking was a History graduate who was very knowledgeable.
As a first time visitor the tour was great.
After the tour we stayed on for another 6 hours and were able to visit most rooms that we wanted to.
Away from the hit exhibits the museum is not as crowded as you might expect.

our guide was young and enthusiastic about art. we learned a lot about art and navigated the crowded louvre with no problems. You do only see a smidgeon of the museum but we were satisfied as it was still three hours or so. definitely worth it!

I need to state from the start - I’m a big fan of tripadvisor and the tours they recommend. So I was very excited and reassured when I booked this tour for my honeymoon in Paris.

First off: previous reviews seem to indicate the tour guides are sticklers for time. We had people rocking up to our 11:30 tour at 11:40 and they were permitted so I wouldn’t sweat it too much. Though we did, because it was 38C outside before our guide moved us under the pyramid.

The tour guide indicated that this was the first time that the Mona Lisa would be at the start of the tour. If I heard the phrase “look at her, she is not smiling” I was going to kill myself. He must have said this about 20 times in the HOUR in took from checking in at security to looking at the aul boot’s face. I understand that he was trying to distract everyone from the queue BUT what would have been more fascinating was a walking commentary on the works of art in the preceding galleries.

Second: you need to appreciate that you are not skipping any internal queues. Apparently the only queue you skip is the external queue as opposed to the groups’ queue. We still queued for about 20 minutes, so weren’t checking in and starting the tour until ~12:15

Third: the tour guide does not give a **** if you have been left behind. My husband and I, plus several other members of the tour were left behind various times due to queue restrictions. No doubt the tour operator will defer to some kind of museum law of the land however if the tour operator had any kind of customer service in mind they would instruct the guide to WAIT on the group members left behind (by Louvre security) and continue the tour so all paying members could “enjoy” what he was saying. It was extremely frustrating having your radio cut out just because the tour guide had dandered off with the lucky 15 people who had managed to charm their way past security while the other 10 of us were left scratching our asses trying to decipher the occasional word that came through the radio.

SUMMARY
Buy your own audio guide and go through the Louvre that way. You don’t need to see the Mona Lisa, she is a plain jane. Go to the Long Gallery and fill your boots, literally everything else is more pfascinating to see.

Enjoy and save yourself some monies :)
It was so informative and well done! The Louvre is a massive place and through this tour we were able to see all of the high points including the Mona Lisa with ease! Thank you!

What and amazing tour this was. What made ALL the difference was our incredible tour guide Nev. She has two degrees one in Art History and is going to do her PHD. Her passion for the arts was second to none and came through as she toured us around the museum for the three hours. It literally flew by and we could have easily followed her around all day listening to the stories and the passion in which she spoke about them. The things she knew and how she relayed it in such a caring and passionate way allowed you to see each piece in a completely different way. Had we not gone on a guide tour, we first of all would not have been able to navigate this gigantic museum and would have walked by these masterpieces aimlessly not understanding the beautiful history on how these pieces were inspired and conceived. We had our 13 year old son with us who is studying art as a concentration in school and he too enjoyed every minute of it. Yes as someone pointed out in another review that the Museum has moved the Mona Lisa to another room as they are renovating hers but the incredible long lines did move fast and was worth the wait. Nev, thanks again for the amazing tour and please don’t ever stop sharing your gift with the world.

Summer was an amazing tour guide. Her passion and her interesting insights and stories were great and the three hours just flew by. I think these kind of tours live and die by the tour guide and we were lucky to have Summer. We did the evening tour which was really awesome and highly recommend. Even our 11 year old daughter thought it was a great tour.

The tour package is great. We had a great "quick" tour of the Louvre. We saw the museum's highlights, learned a lot from a terrific guide, and learned our way around the expansive museum. After the tour we struck out on our own to go back and see more of the areas we were most interested in. Highly recommend.

Booked this to ensure I could get in to the museum with minimal fuss. This convenience comes at a cost.

We met near the arch across the road from
The museum. We were given an ear plug for listening to the tour guide.

We entered and the place was quite full. The guide seemed to keep us moving but still gave us plenty of information.

I loved how the museum is set out and they are currently renovating areas something that must be happening on an ongoing basis.

We did the highlights only but it gave us a great idea of the museum.

Tour Is worth it if you want to skip the
Lines.

I Have been to the Louvre several times but my Husband had never been so we opted for a private tour and it was so very worth the price!! Our Guide spoke English very well (He was Irish!), very knowledgeable and interesting to listen to. He got us to all the most important pieces and was so helpful and kind with my Husband who has some mobility issues; found elevators and helped us navigate a huge building. Would do this again and again every time I come!! Thank you!

This is a must do in Paris. Could you wait in line and wander around by yourself.... sure.... but if you want to have a fantastic experience do the tour. It is very well organized and gets you to all of the highlights over the 1.5 hours. Also packed with a lot of history and insight otherwise we wouldn’t have know. Finally, Christina V is an excellent guide. Very knowledgeable, personable and just great.

I love to learn. And that is what you do when you go in a skip the line tour with a guide that has a masters in art.My whole family was fascinated the way she entwined art and history as it had just happened yesterday.
Wonderful tour.

I highly recommend booking 'skip the line' tours well in advance, especially during peak season when some of the sights sell out. Our tour guide, Abrahim, was exceptional - very knowledgeable about history and art and was a real pleasure. We covered lots of ground during the 3 hours and I was happy to have good walking shoes. I suggest booking a morning tour as you can stay in the museum after the tour ends and explore on your own. There's so much to see, it would take days, or even weeks, to take it all in.

If your time in Paris is limited, and you still want to be able to see some key pieces, this is the tour for you. Since the Louvre is so massive, we could have spent days looking around and never stumbled across the biggies. Our guide Fab was expert at scooting our group around edges of the huge crowds and up to the artwork. She also had an obvious love and enthusiasm for the works, which made the tour very enjoyable. The only hiccup was the spotty microphone to our headsets, which was distracting and should be improved upon. Otherwise, this was a great intro to the Louvre. Fab also mentioned that we were free to roam around on our own after the tour, which I wish I'd known before, as I made plans for right afterwards. Worth the money.

We had a wonderful time today in our group tour. We have three young children and Nev our guide had us captivated throughout. She is very friendly and knowledgeable with a double Masters degree and now doing a PhD in art history. She taught us about the history of the building and also the finer points of some of the key art pieces at the Louvre. Nev certainly made our day in Paris very memorable.
This was an amazing tour! Our guide Allister was very knowledgeable and passionate about art! I would highly recommend this tour!

City Wonders cancelled on us last minute (~ 2 days before) due to "unforeseen circumstances". Let me translate -- either they didn't buy tickets far enough in advance or they didn't have enough people on the tour. The late cancellation left us in the lurch, no advance tickets were available nor were any tours, more or less making visiting the Louvre impossible.

Skip the line tour worth every penny on this one. Walked past a HUGE line of tourists and strolled right in with tour guide Laura who was about the best tour guide I’ve ever had. Her expansive knowledge of history and art, paired with her down to earth personality made the tour pure delight!

FYI, if you don't have tickets when you get there, don't stand in that huge line outdoor, or even buy tickets from the guys that sell them and tell you you can skip the line. The Louvre is amazing, there's lots to see, you probably need a whole day there. The mall have some good deals, we bought wine and food chocolate there

In many of our trips we choose City Tours for sight seeing the various attractions. In Paris recently we took a tour to the Louvre that we booked in advance to our trip. We enjoyed this attraction immensely probably one of the best parts of our trip not only of what we saw but our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable of the exhibits and delivered an explanation that was interesting and thorough. Fabricia at the Louvre delivered a presentation on Napoleon lll and his apartment, Venus, Nike and the Mona Lisa, Fabricia was exciting, enjoyed talking about each and expanded on various parts of the presentation one of the best tour guides we have had.

The skip the line feature was definitely a plus. It saved us about 1.5 hours in line. The tour organizers were very efficient in getting us into groups and giving our headsets. Kudos for that.

Unfortunately this tour was frustrating and disappointing based largely on the tour guide. Abdul was very pleasant and very knowledgeable. For some art lovers this tour would be perfect. But for me it was just information overload. My son was looking forward to this museum. He now has no desire to see it again.

Our guide Anastasia, was fantastic. Highly knowledgeable, and a pleasure to follow, we got to see everything we wanted and more, in only roughly 3 hours, which is impressive given the sheer size of the Louvre. Was also great to not have to queue, walking straight in to the museum. Saw many people struggling with maps and directions, it really is enormous and a guide is essential. Highly recommend this company, and especially Anastasia.

This was an excellent tour that was very informative and made me appreciate the museum more. Our guide was Alexander and he was extremely knowledgable and provided great information about the art that we viewed. I'm so glad that I went with this tour because I probably would've gotten lost since the museum is so large and the map was confusing. Thankfully Alex was able to direct us to the "greatest hits" of the museum. Highly recommended!

Louvre is just a fascinating place with all the huge area and the outstanding arts open for the public. Greek sculptures, paintings, Mona Lisa, Rembrandt, Davinci, etc.It's just a mus to go place in Paris. Holds the history of years and years, including the apartments of Napoleon III.

Our guide, Adam, is what made this tour fantastic. The Louvre is huge and our teenager does not have a love for the art.....yet. Adam was extremely knowledgeable yet made it fun and humorous. I wish we had him for every tour we did on Paris. “Team Adam” really made the tour the best. Thanks Adam!

This was an excellent tour and well worth the cost. We were able to see the highlights of the museum with a well informed guide. We learned amazing details of the art pieces and history of the artists. We had visited the Louvre before on our own. We missed so much as do- it- yourselfers. We did not understand much as we wandered the museum on our won. This gave us a rich background for the museum.

Our guide Laura was amazing. We enjoyed all the information shared by someone clearly passionate about art and the Louvre. She navigated us beautifully through the crowds to see the highlights like Venus di Milo and the Mona Lisa. This tour was the perfect amount of time for our teenagers. You can elect to stay in the museum after your tour ends. Be warned...if you book through Viator as we did, there is some vital information missing from your voucher. You must be at the meeting point well before the scheduled tour time. If your voucher says 9:45, be there by 9:15. The group is on one group ticket and if you are late there is no individual ticket to acquire on your own. This tour company went out of their way to accommodate late clients but it did require rescheduling in some cases. I highly recommend this tour.
Fabrizia was a wonderful guide, passionate and knowledgeable. She brought the art to life with much history and stories along the tour.

I wish I had days to spend in the Louvre! So sad it was only one evening but our guide, Manny was beyond knowledgeable. He took us to Mona Lisa and Venus DiMilo as promised but also many other sculptures and paintings that were beyond beautiful.

Totally wish we got Mannys number so we could do a private tour with him! Truly the best guide and very attune to his audience. Recommend you ask for Manny!

We knew the Louvre would be busy but even being such a huge place it was still very crowded. Our guide Julien did a fabulous job of keeping us all together, explaining in great detail all the major pieces as we worked our way through, and keeping us thoroughly entertained for the full 3 hours. We got to see all the important works including a battle through ‘hell room’ to see Mona Lisa up close and personal. We did feel a little rushed at times but I don’t think we had much choice. There was so much to get through in just 3 hours. Really enjoyed the tour and as usual it was topped off by a wonderful guide.

Our tour guide (forgive me I can't recall his name - the Spaniard), was an absolute savant. His shared his love for art, history, and France on the 3 hour tour. We got to see all the major artworks, and were all educated on several periods of history. It was an amazing experience and I'm glad I did this. Otherwise, I'd have been lost in the Louvre for hours on end trying to find things.

This review is not a slam on the tour guide. We visited the museum on May 2, a Wednesday, after the museum had been closed for 2 consecutive days. The museum was horribly crowded to the extent that it was extremely difficult to move with a tour guide. We had to stand in line for 15 minutes to get into the relatively large room which holds the Mona Lisa. We couldn’t ever get very close to the painting because the room was so packed with people. Even though the museum is huge you had trouble moving around especially when near the popular art pieces. Our tour guide was really frazzled by the crowds as well. I think it would have been a very nice tour if we could have been there on a less busy day.

We booked our tour of the Louvre Museum through Trip Advisor - Skip The Line Tours. The actual tour provider was “City Wonders Ltd”. Our English speaking guide was Julien and for the next 3.5 hours he lead a rather large group of 23 people through the highlights of this massive treasure chest of the world’s art.

Julien was fun, entertaining and knowledgeable of the art we visited and the Louvre itself. He weaved a story of each of the great works, including the artist, the techniques, it’s place in history and it’s importance to the art world. How Julien did all this while keeping track of 23 people is a tribute to his expertise as a guide.

The museum was quite crowded in some places, (even mid-morning on a Thursday in early May). But Julien gave us ample warning before we entered these sections and lead us through the spaces while gathered us for his next presentation. Three hours 45 minutes later we gathered one last time to say goodbye - we had seen every work he promised and then some. Voilà!

Our family took this tour, 2 seniors, 1 adult and two girls age 8. We all enjoyed the tour and our guide, Anastasia was excellent. She made it easy to get into the Louvre and see the best of the sites with excellent commentary. Highly recommend for all.

This tour exceeded my expectations by far! It was so informative and FUN! If you go definitely ask for tour guide ADAM. I've been on a lot of museum tours and Adam is the best guide I've ever had. My sister did the walk through of the Louvre with a friend and I think she regrets not going on the tour with us. Adam seems to know all the good spots to view the art and knows when exhibits are closed and open and what time of day to see them in order to avoid too much crowding.Thank you Adam!
Sarah from Vermont

Adam of “Team Adam” from City Wonders was AWESOME!!!! Very informative and interesting and kept the kids attention throughout the tour. Was very enthusiastic and energetic. Would highly recommend this tour and would definitely recommend asking for Adam if you can. Was well worth the money and bypassed long lines. DO IT!!!
Our tour guide Adam deserves a raise! He provided a lot of good knowledge on many exhibits, including ones in other museums around the world.

Today we were part of Team Adam, lead by a dynamic personality, Adam. He was knowledgeable and made it entertaining to learn about many the Louvre's halls. Skipping the line saves hours and you could easily get overwhelmed in the museum, Adam got us through the throngs and to important pieces, including the big 3.

We had booked the tour for 9:45 am on April 15th. We were on time, although the leader did not have enough audio set! There was another couple from Texas with the same situation. She just left us without any help and nice explanation! We called the operator 3 times and waited for two hours to give us a solution or a refund! They offered a tour for two days after, when we had a flight to Italy!!! They totally screwed the first day of our honeymoon! After contacting them several times in few days to get a refund, they just offered us a credit for the same tour, although we have to use it in 6 months!!!! This is worthless! We travelled such a long way from Canada!

Our guide Lawrence was fantastic navigating The Louvre with ease. We would not have seen all we did if left to our own devices! So busy and yet it was stress free and very enjoyable. Highly recommended and thank you for creating many happy memories for us sharing your knowledge and enthusiasm from a true Parisian

Very very good and informative tour. I was visiting Paris the first time and a visit to the Louvre was definitely a must do. I had less time as I was only there for one weekend, and this suited my purpose completely. I was able to see the prime attractions of the museum and apart from that the tour guide was very knowledgeable and explained in details of everything we were seeing. Definitely worth the time and the money spent :)

A wonderful experience. I looked forward to this tour, but it was more than I hoped for. Traveling with friends in a first time visit to Paris, we looked forward to seeing Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo. I knew a three hour tour would be a small glimpse of the museum. It was more! Our guide, Lucia, was knowledgeable, charming, and efficient! She brought to life the art, the history, and the character of the art, the artists, and the Louvre. Timing and pace was managed very well. We covered an incredibly large amount of the museum while never feeling rushed or hurried. The tour was well managed, punctual, professional, headsets clear, and the guide Lucia perfect. Well done!

I thought this was an excellent tour. The Louvre is just so massive. Reuben was an excellent guide - knowledgeable, entertaining and funny. The three hour tour was just right to get me orientated to the museum and to give me confidence to explore further.

Our narrator was full of knowledge. She knew things about the very crevases of the Louvre Museum. This was our first visit, and after a few years will definately return. By then, they will have excavated even more grounds to learn about.

My wife and I booked this tour of the Louvre. Violet, our guide was simply the best. Very knowledgeable AND entertaining. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience, including bypassing the long wait lines.

We took this guided tour yesterday (Sunday 27th January). Our guide Manni/Manny was brilliant. He made the tour enjoyable and made the exhibitions relatable. He was extremely knowledgable about both the Louvre and Paris itself. He ensured we came away feeling like we had covered the museum highlights along with time to take photos at key points. The use of the head phone radio system made it easy to listen from a good vantage point. He was also easy to locate and follow due to his hair which was a massive help in crowded rooms (as below)! A great tour which will be recommended.
Thank you ! It was an incredible journey and worth the price we paid . Our Guide was very informative and gave us plenty of time to adore the masterpieces.

These tours are definitely worth the little bit extra to skip the que's!

Our tour guide Adam was the best guide we had throughout our whole stay in Paris. He was very approachable if you had a question about the art and also made what he was saying interesting and funny. He is very knowledgable and passionate about the history of the art that was in the Louvre and this was reflected throughout the whole tour!

Would recommend Adam to anyone wishing to have a guided tour of the Louvre.

We had a fabulous tour by Violet who is an experienced, energetic guide. She has a Masters degree in art history and can talk to the history, architecture and art collection. She hits the must-see pieces but goes beyond that to include a wide variety of works.

I highly recommend a skip the line tour for a first-time visitor to tackle this humongous museum as it can be overwhelming. Our guide handled the logistics, which took the stress out of it.

The whole tour took three hours but it went fast due to Violet’s wit and wisdom.

Merci Beaucoup!

Maura and Patrick
Went to the Louvre, had an amazing guide: Daniel the Irish dude! Our experience would not have been the same without him! Thank you for making an awesome venue that much better!

This experience was great! It was easy to find the tour operator and get going in the Louvre. We walked right in and skipped all lines. Abby was our tour guide and was great at giving funny and relevant details. Didn't feel long but also felt like we saw everything we needed to at the museum as first time visitors. Highly recommend!

We were recently in Paris and participated in the skip the line Louvre tour . There are not enough compliments to describe how good Evana was as a guide. We learned so much in our 2.5 hours. Her knowledge was so impressive and she share it with style. Thank you so much for making our Louvre tour so a great learning experience.

We really enjoyed this tour. Our guide, Claudia, was passionate and knowledgeable, picking out highlights from the Louvre and giving lots of information about the building and it's history.
If you want to know the detail of lots of the paintings in the Louvre this is maybe not the tour for you, but if you want to find out about the building, it's background, some of the key pieces (paintings and sculptures) then you will enjoy it.
Claudia is a great story teller and shared these well to weave in the technical and historical details of the exhibits she took us to.
Skipping the line meant we were in quickly, with no queueing and able to make the most of the 3 hour trip.
Well worth the money.
I was a little disappointed w the tour because it said small group but we were over 15 people. The guide was good though

My, (adult), daughter and I had the most amazing guide and,luckily, a small group of 5. Our guide had a Masters in Art History from the Sorbonne, and was originally from Boston. He had great stories and information that made the paintings and sculptures so much more interesting than I've ever found them to be! With anything that you do, the person or guide will make all of the difference. We were so fortunate to have spent our day with Lee. I've done other City Wonder tours that were awful due to poor guides (see my review of Versailles). Thank you Lee for sharing your knowledge with us! It was both interesting and great fun!

This tour exceeded our expectations. Our guide was Francisa and she was a wealth of information. She made this tour just so meaningful and interesting. If we had gone on our own there is so much that we would not had known,
We had absolutely no problem in regards to tickets - we printed them off at home - when we arrived at the meeting area, they did not even need our tickets as they had our name on the list, It was simple and seamless, We recommend this tour

Daniel the Irish Guy was fantastic. We were in a group of 14 and had a ear piece to hear him even in the crowded museum. It wouldn't have been nearly as informative or fun without him. It was 3 hours which was perfect. Showed us the best pieces and had informative explanations. He had a passion for what he does.

Sorry I did not get the name of our guide but she was awesome. Wonderful 3 hour tour, she was very knowlegdeable and easy to listen to. The Louvre itself is amazing and vast. A must see in Paris. Well organized and Louvre has restaurants and washrooms under it...which is good to know in advance.

I enjoyed a wonderful three hour tour of the Louvre with Adam from City Wonders. I learned so much and could never had navigated this museum on my own. Adam was very genuine and an excellent tour guide. He was well qualified and made our entire tour interesting, entertaining and informative. My day at the Louvre was one of the highlights of my trip to Paris all thanks to Team Adam!! Merci beaucoup Adam!

We should have checked to see if there were lines before purchasing this tour. We were given our tickets and a museum map outside the Le Louvre and told how to read the map. So not really any purpose to this tour. Apart from to pay more money for entrance

We were met by Kristina under the Arc de Triumph du Carrousel. Kristina introduced herself as being from Romania and had studied at Cambridge and UC London gaining a MA in Art History. She had been a guide for 4 years, specialising in The Louvre and Versailles. She then explaining what we would see over the next 3 hours.
We started with the old Fortress and progressed through the major galleries, seeing some of the great works of art. Mona Lisa and Madonna on the Rocks by Da Vinci amongst others. Sculptures by Michaelangelo and too many others to name.
We ended the tour with a brief tour of the State Apartments of Bonepart III.
Kristina’s entheasium for her subject came through leaving us all wanting to know and see more but sadly time eluded us.
This is a tour not to be missed. Highly Recommended.

We did the 3hr tour and our guide Natalie was fantastic. Natalie was extremely knowledgable and knew her way around the museum like it was her second home.

We were very pleased with the tour.
My husband and I had the most amazing time all of the tours were so incredible The artwork the jewelry everything is amazing

For the money vs the time you have to wait in line , it's worth it to buy this tour. In July the main line was very long, we skipped it and waited in the group line for about 15 mins which I would consider normal(there is security check you have to go through). The museum was very crowded but our tour guide managed to show us the main pieces and explain the history. If you have the option, don't go in summer you would probably enjoy the museum better. We stayed after the tour ended and looked at more paintings.

Our tour guide gets a 5 star rating - the tour organizer, City Wonders, gets a zero.
We were told to arrive at the meeting location at 6:15 (15 minutes before the start of the 6:30 pm tour). On July 4th, at 6:15 there were probably 75-100 people standing around waiting for a City Wonders representative to appear. That happened at 7:00 pm. Before he arrived, several people called the contact number on my voucher but only reached a recording.

The representative didn't have a sign or any City Wonders uniform and the start to the tour was chaotic to say the least. We didn't get into the museum until after 7:30. Fortunately, our guide was excellent and partly made up for this disastrous start.

Since we were unable to compete the full three hour tour (the museum was only open for two more hours) I asked for a 50% refund and they only gave me back $29 for my entire group. That is insulting.

I did not enjoy this tour at all. It’s always 50/50 there will be an entrance line, but on the afternoon of June 27, 2018, there was not much of one that I could see. Thus the major reason you pay, to skip a non existant line, was negated. By the way, skip the line means skip the entrance line - accomplished for us via a side entrance, 1/2 a mile from where the tour originated. It does not mean you will get any where near the Mona Lisa without waiting in a line.

The major reason for my dissatisfaction is this tour company uses outdated headsets. If you enjoy listening to static, and the constant breathing of the tour guide in your ear, this is the tour for you.

Additionally, our guide was not interesting. His stories and presentation was dull and bland. If I recall, he said it was his second of 3 tours that day, though we might have been the third.

The day we arrived in Paris, we had nothing arranged for the Eiffel Tower, but we walked right up and got to the top in less than 1/2 hour. We had similar luck at the Sacré-Coeur, and at Notre Dame. Should I pass this way again, I would take my chances with the entrance line for the Louvre. I could have seen just as much, as well as had time to linger over some of the better pieces I saw that day. Most in passing, however, as we were in a guided tour, and it was made clear that one must keep with the group.

We opted for an advance booking prior to our trip to Paris and other cities in France.
We chose to do this "Skip The Line" tour just as a precautionary move as we knew the standard tours have a long wait ime to get in.
Our guide met us right at the ticket area for the Paris City Vsion and there were ( 8 ) of us for this tour. As we were getting set up with our headsets, the Big Bus was loading up the 90 or more people that were on the regular Lourve trip to deliver them to the already long line of tourists waiting to enter the museum.
We just walked about a hundred yards hearing all the history of the museum to the entrance and walked right in through the private entry way for our tour.
I certainly would recommend this "Skip The Line" tour even though it is a bit more expensive. My time is more valuable than a few extra dollars to bypass the long wait time for getting in to this wonderful museum.

We arrived an hour before the Louvre opened (opens at 9am) and were second in line in the skip-the-line line. There were four lines: one for museum pass holders, one for skip-the-line tickets, one for people who had to purchase tickets, and one for people in wheelchairs, strollers, etc. By 9am, all lines were very, very long. Security personnel checked our tickets while in line, then we went through bag check, and then they checked our tickets again to enter the museum inside. KEEP YOUR TICKETS. In the early afternoon, they started to shut off parts of the museum with no explanation. To get to the other side we had to exit and reenter, and we needed to show our tickets to do so.
Advice: Purchase these tickets in advance to save a good amount of time, and get there early to be near the front of the line; we saved maybe 30 minutes at least. Get there early and go straight to the Mona Lisa and any other exhibits you want to see. We were able to get an unobstructed picture of the Mona Lisa and spend a few minutes enjoying it before a crowd of people started to arrive. We ate at the terrace cafe (forgot the name), sandwiches were good, the sales people were very nice and spoke some English, and the views were beautiful.

This was the perfect way to tour The Louvre. Our guide, Alistair, was amazing. He was personable and knew so much about The Louvre and everything in it. The time seemed to fly by. When was the last time you felt like that in a museum??
Our after hours tour of the Louvre was fantastic thanks to guide-extraordinaire Inna. She provided great insights we would have missed without her.

We purchased the skip the line pass from our hotel concierge and it was well worth it. Once inside, we didn't have to stand in another line to buy tickets to the special Delacroix exposition. Also, another great tip is.....on Wednesdays the museum is open later so going in the late afternoon avoids a lot of the crowds.

If you can only spend one day here, this is the way to do it. This museum is so large, that you could spend a week and not see everything. This was worth the money just to skip the long entry line. That said, having a guide to take you directly to many of the noteworthy pieces was truly worth the money! It saved us from wandering aimlessly.

So looking forward to this. Really poor guide. So many people it was useless to try to see anything. Guide focused on on one person. Small group tour was 15 people. No historical context. Had so many great tours on the trip. This , not so much. Tour guide never said his name! Good reason!

With the Louvre being one of the most visited place in Paris and in the world the line tends to be extremely long. With the skip the line tickets we by passed the huge sea of people and got right in. The Louvre is huge, comprised with 75k pieces of art work its impossible to see everything in just a few hours, but this tour does a great job of visiting the most important pieces as well as important artifacts of human history. the tour began just by the arch outside of the Louvre. My wife and I were extremely excited for the tour and once we met our guide Adam we knew that it was going to be a great tour. Adam led our group through the museum starting with ancient history leading up to more modern art. Adam showed us all the big pieces the Louvre has to offer and got us right up in front of all the art which we really appreciated it. After taking several tours through Europe, this one was the best one we were on and Adam was a huge contributing factor to that.

If you are undecided on which tour to take, book this one and hopefully you get Adam!

We are not huge museum fans but wanted to see the Mona Lisa. Because of the knowledge that Adam had about so many different exhibits we now have a completely different attitude. He gave us a background of society at the time many things were made, painted etc which completely explained the why and how of the pieces. Sooo interesting. Highly recommend this tour!

We were so pleased we did this tour. The guide was very knowledgeable and was passionate about art. She guided us through the Lourve which was very crowded on the day we went, Monday and showed us the highlights and more famous pieces. This was excellent given that we only had a short period of time. There are so many passage ways and levels to the Lourve that we would not have seen the same had we done the tour on our own.

My partner and I wanted to see the Louvre for the experience but not really into art too much. Our guide (can’t remember her name) provided us with a fantastic tour and made the experience one of our favourites! We had skip the line tickets which are most definitely worth it and we got to see all the main attractions of the Louvre including the Mona Lisa and our guide provided us insight into many works of the museum, she was very knowledgeable and we had a great day!
Although crowded and rainy Adam turned the day into a joy! The tour and insight was concise, focused but yet fun!

The tour guide was informative and kind. The tour was amazing and enlightening. The guide was able to answer most questions and constantly checked in, with our group.
The only dissatisfier is that we waiting 10-15 minutes for late arrivals. We met outside and the temperatures were very cold.
I would definitely refer this tour to any family or friends.

The meeting spot was easily defined, but someone was late with passes and microphones, so we waited in the blowing rain under the structure. 5-10 minutes late seems longer when it is raining. We loved the tour guide - and the use of the ear phones, she was knowledgeable and attempted to guide the group to the best views of the works of art. She incorporated history into why paintings were seen as important or not. She was patient and offered recommendations for what others could see and do once the tour ended. Would recommend this guided tour, but would not do it on a busy weekend morning. See if you can get an evening tour, when the museum is less crowded.

This was THE best tour we've ever been on and Susan was absolutely fantastic. She showed us all of the major things to see and as we are not super big art people but she pointed out all of the cool stuff in the paintings and sculptures that we would've otherwise missed. She also kept things very interesting! She also had some great stories to go with the pieces that she showed us. Her tour gave us a great overview of the Louvre, efficiently. I can see how people spend hours there and with only a day and a half in Paris, we didn't have that luxury (plus there is just so much to see!) With this tour, we felt that we were able to really see the Louvre. We went back and forth about doing a tour before we booked this and after doing this tour, I would absolutely recommend taking a tour. Otherwise, you could very easily wander for hours "seeing things" but not truly appreciating them.

Our plane arrived late in Paris so we missed the 11am tour. We stuck around waiting for the 230 tour but it never happened. I contacted city wonders. They refuse to refund us. The late plane arrival was out of our control. So city wonders took our $$. We got nothing in return
Pick up of tickets no problems. Skipped the queue/ guide was knowledgeable and we really enjoyed the visit. We saw different parts of the muesem not normally seen.
We liked that it took us in the highlights of the museum as it was so large and we had a limited time to partake.

We’re so glad to we booked this Louvre tour during our Paris weekend. Marie was a delightful art historian and tour guide. City Wonders checked us in and Marie expertly guided us through the underground group skip-the-line entrance and then the free lockers for our heavy wet coats from the rain. We were provided headphones to hear the tour and instructions as we weaved through the Sunday crowd. Marie’s intelligent observations and supplemental pics from her phone helped us understand the relevance and great significance of many of the key sculptures and paintings throughout the Louvre. With only half a day to spend at the Louvre, this tour made sure we made the most of our visit. Highly recommended!!

The start of the tour was a shambles and required us to wait 25 minutes whilst the operator sourced enough headsets for their guests. Don’t bother with this tour if you want to see the Mona Lisa close up; the guide was not prepared to commit to queuing with everyone else and so we were left with looking at the picture from a distance over the heads of others and being ushered to move along by the Louvre security. It was not explained why and maybe it was the lost 25 minutes. It was a shame for the guide who was clearly embarrassed as she knew her subject and passionate about the art.

Guide company was a disaster. Unorganized, understaffed, difficult to determine who and where they were. One person did her best to check in 4 different tours without a list of each tour using her cell phone. When the guide did show up 30 minutes after the tour was to start he announced because of a ticketing problem he was not sure that we would be allowed to enter. Not a great way to start the tour.
The guide was very knowledgeable and helpful but I would never use the tour company again because of their terrible administration.

It was a great experience! Our tour guide, Manuel, was the best! He made it fun and interesting! In addition, he was very knowledgeable! He took us to see the main arts and gave us lots of good tips for Paris in general! I would definitely recommend this event to all!

What a fabulous tour!!
Our guide kept things light but extremely informative.
Well worth the cost, thoroughly enjoyed it.
Our guide Anna was superb. She was pleasant and poured her heart out while giving the tour. We had a great experience at Louvre. Highly recommend the tour.
It was great! Violet ( not really her French name) was extremely knowledgeable and informative. I learned a lot. Who knew the Mona Lisa was a man!
Claire was so knowledgeable and passionate about French history. I would have just wandered through and never appreciated all there is to see. Skipping the long lines was also worth every penny!

Our guide Thierry was excellent. He answered any question along the tour. Due to closure of a part of the Louvre he had to improvise and was great in guiding us around to see the significant art pieces.
Natalie our guide was highly informative and made sure she showed us and explained to us as much as she was able along with all the popular pieces with great information about them and their history.
Flor our guide was excellent! She was funny and knowledgeable and guided us thru on a very busy day due to the holiday in France.
Just a wonderful experience, its very busy so booking ahead is a good idea the que moves quick but its all worth the wait.
It is so well worth it to take a guided experience and skip the line ticket!! Our guide was very good. The tour was 3 hours, bring some water!
Really worth the time and money. Great art, history. Beautiful place. Defo do skip d que . Could go back again to see more.

Our tour added such depth to the experience of the Louve I wouldn’t consider going it alone!
The museum is so large that’s it’s impossible to tour solo and even see half the highlights you have on the tour.
The guide was excellent provided interesting information and very knowledgeable on the Louvre Museum and its contents

I had a great experience with the tour. Our guide was very knowledgable. She explained the history behind the paintings and sculptures in great details.

I was slightly disappointed with the fact that modern French art, especially those done during Napoleon III, got a lot of attention but we did not go to the Egyptian side at all. But it was mainly my fault because I didn't read the description of the trip well.

Another request - NOT a complain - it would be great if the guide could sometimes offer to take the participants' pictures since it is not easy to ask other random people. I did a city tour that I booked through TripAdvisor and the guide there was very enthusiastic in helping with pictures. I totally understand that it is NOT part of the guide's job description. But given that most tourists like taking pictures with the famous art pieces, it will be a nice bonus.
The tour was as described and I highly recommend. Anna, our guide was very enthusiastic and helpful. Made the most of our 3 hours
Maxim was so knowledgeable and sensitive to everyone’s needs. Great overview of the museum. The crowds are large so it was helpful to skip the lines. 3 hours was the right amount of time.

A “semi-private” tour of the Louvre with an English speaking art historian was the description! How could I go wrong? Let me count the ways…..
Inju (?……she said it was a Korean name) introduced herself, giving no further details of her academic or cultural background. It was immediately apparent that English was not her first or second language…many vocalized pauses while she searched for the right English word..and stilted sentence structure. Her comments
on the exhibits mostly reflected the written guides posted (in English) by the Museum. She showed no enthusiasm for her subject matter or the job at hand.
After 45 minutes, I handed back my audio squawkbox and earpiece, quite sure that I could better tour this amazing collection of the world’s art on my own. I can only feel sympathy for the 11 people I left behind, and wonder how many of them lasted the remaining two hours.
And no way to lodge a complaint directly with City Wonders Ltd or viator.com, apparently a “TripAdvisor company”. The No Refund policy is very clear. Sad that the tour was not as promised.
Flora was a great guide with a great sense of humor! She kept us entertained to the very end! Fascinating tour with a detailed historical perspective.
This was one of our favorite experiences in Paris. Our guide Florence was so informative. We saw the highlights of this enormous museum

Claire was amazing!! She answered every question, kept track of all 23 of us and even recommended suggestions for places to eat - I asked and got a great answer, ate at the recommendation and it was awesome. We must be the odd ones out but my family and I (my parents and my 10 and 12 year old kids) did not enjoy this tour and we would not recommend it. It is a huge group - the tour guide cannot possibly keep track of everyone, and ours didn't have a flag or anything to help us follow her, and the crowds are massive - so the first thing that happened was that our family, another family, and another couple all got separated from the guide and the rest of the group. For probably close to ten minutes. I had believed I heard her say something about security so we went to the front of the security line and basically begged them that we were in a tour group and they let us through, thankfully. Once we had caught back up, the very first piece of art shown to the group was the statue of a woman breastfeeding her father, with her nipple in his mouth. I get that it's famous and depicts an act "of love" borne of desperation, but I think it's a bit jarring to start a group tour off with something so, well, gross. I saw another group member shaking her head in disgust. I myself was there with my own dad. It was just a really bizarre, awkward way to start the journey off. It also wasn't clear why it was started this way - was this the oldest part of the museum? I don't know; perhaps this was explained during the security line we missed.

There was almost nowhere to sit, a TON of stairs - there should really be a warning about this on the booking site, like there is for the catacombs (If there is, I apologize for missing it) - the group was so large that if you had to go to the bathroom you'd be lost. I also couldn't really understand the guide - she spoke very good English but still had a hefty accent, and there was a LOT of background noise from the crowds and she didn't really enunciate things very clearly. A lot of the information given that I **could** hear and understand was also just a bit too detailed - learning about the advent of the use of darkness and light to show location (as one example) is more "art class" for me, not "historical/cultural significance of this particular piece." We left less than halfway through and I found it more enjoyable to just sort of see what pieces caught my eye and then read their plaques on my own. Again, perhaps we were the odd ones out. But for us this tour was difficult to follow, exhausting, and not particularly fascinating.

We joined Adam as guide on our Skip The Line tour today Thursday, December 19, 2019. We had advance notice that the tour was delayed 1 hr because of the ongoing Paris strikes. And it was still a perfect tour lasting a full 3+ hours. Adam is a Canadian native, trained in Nuclear Engineering, who has followed his first love of art and has worked with CityWonder for years. His sense of humor, knowledge of facts, and skill in presenting the facts results in a memorable tour in which you'll see highlights of the Louvre (including the Apollo room which recently reopened), and learn a foundation of facts about each piece of art and/or the artist that paints a truly masterful picture. And with this deeper understanding of each piece of art on the tour comes a finer appreciation of the artwork, whether you're a novice or an expert. Adam will lead you to the best places to see a particular piece of art; show you a series of other pieces leading up to the Mona Lisa; quiz you to decide which wing of Winged Victory of Samothrace was replaced; demonstrate the how and why of heads vs busts vs missing noses and defacing...and much more. The radio headsets worked perfectly. Adam's group had about 25 folks from around the world. CityWonder tours were excellent in assisting me in finding a misplaced booking confirmation. All in all, my wife and I highly recommend this guided tour for an introduction to the Louvre.

I would highly recommend this tour! But if you've never been to the Louvre, take the 5 minutes we should have taken to figure out exactly where the meet up place is.

"Laura" informed us about so many different aspects of the architecture, sculptures and paintings in the Louvre that I am still astonished by her special talent of being both informative and enthusiastic.This is one vacation I will never forget! Bravo, Trip Advisor, for having Laura as one of your guides!
Very professional and organizer..tours guide were wonderful. Guides help transcend the period and time of the museum exhibits

This worked out quite well for my friends and I. The first two hours we saw a lot of key things that definitely made the tour worth it. The last hour was more focused on some specific type of art that I was not as interested in so a two hour tour would have worked out better for me but still a good value and I would recommend it.
The guide was amazing and gave us great information. We had the first tour of the day which gave us enough time to visit the Mona Lisa.. Line for the Mona Lisa is very long...

I believe our tour guide's name was Katrina. She was great the entire time and highlighted some of her favorite works in addition to the famous ones. She had a deep knowledge of the history of the museum and the artwork, which made it much more interesting. We came during a less busy time of the year and the line to get in without the tour was still very long, so I would advise paying for skip the line. The tour was around 2 hours then since admission was included, we were free to roam the museum after if we wanted.

Francesca was a good guide who had a good understanding of European history. It was quite a large group ~10 people which was difficult in such a busy place. I would recommend if you want an express tour of the Louvre!

My wife and I participated in this group tour led by Alex, who did a great job. Not knowing a lot about how to differentiate art, particularly paintings, we’d hope to gain insights. Alex did not disappoint with his knowledge on several key pieces of art from sculptures to paintings he was clearly a student of the arts.

Although the Musée was crowded it was nice to move as a group and learn from each other. Highly recommend.

Fab was a wonderful tour guide and this was an amazing experience. She was very knowledgeable and the Louvre is HUGE. This is exactly what I wanted to get all the highlights because I know I would have missed them otherwise.

Violete was an excellent guide. Informative as well as entertaining. We breezed through the museum on our own special tour with Violete not only pointing out the most important works but also providing obscure facts about the artists or the history of the art. The time savings alone made it worth every penny! Fly by all the waiting tourists and get a personal and professional guide who know's the ropes!
What a great way to see an epic and huge museum. The booking went flawless and our guide had amazing English as well as knowledge of the Louvre and it’s collections. Highly recommend

Our first visit to the Louvre was great. Adam did an outstanding job of directing us through the overwhelming art exhibits. He was very knowledgeable and personable. Can’t say enough about him. I would highly recommend City Wonders company and especially Adam. You will not be disappointed.

We had an excellent tour guide, Alex. Very educated, articulate and spoke very clear. Spent 3 hours with him in our group of 12.
We marveled at his enthusiasm for art history.
His stories were so interesting.
Again Viator, another great experience.

I was initially on the fence about booking a guided tour of the Louvre, but eventually decided to do so given the enormity of the place. Nancy was a great guide: full of energy, curiosity and knowledge about all the important paintings and artworks that we saw, and all within schedule! Very impressive and definitely felt I was in good hands the whole time. We were given plenty of time for bathroom and walking breaks, and despite the hordes of visitors we never felt lost. Extra bonus: she saw Beyonce's Apeshit video and could relate to me on that level so definitely A+ for that as well! Much recommended, you can't really go wrong with Nancy or City Wonders for such a great and memorable overview of this important piece of world heritage.

The tour was great. Our guide was exceptional. He was full of background information and interesting anecdotes about the artwork and the artists. My wife and I enjoyed it immensely. We certainly recommend it.

Felix was awesome....entertaining, informative and passionate about the Arts.
Couldn’t have asked for better and would do it again.
Skip the line is the only way to go!

A very informative and entertaining tour. Adam catered to our every need - best of which were his strategies to best view popular pieces, witty jokes and analogies relating the artworks of antiquity to contemporary phenomenons and most importantly his tasteful and insightful perspectives on the major pieces. Thoroughly enjoyed the 3 hours with not a moment of dullness! Highly recommended!

Robert was our guide for a 3 hour tour of the Louvre. He is passionate about his guidance. He builds the story of the complexities of painting over time and as it relates to a French history. With 16 people in the group, he kept us all together. I am especially appreciative of the extra care for my wife who walks slowly and has difficulty with all the different levels in the Louvre. He tried calling her princess, but she corrected him that her self appointed title is empress. After that he referred to her has Your Majesty. Wonderful sense of humor. He made the tour fly by in a crowded museum.

An excellent 3-hour tour which provided great insight into some of the key exhibits. The skip the line entry was quick and easy, but what made the tour was the knowledge and helpfulness of our guide, Adam.

Our guide, Violette was extremely knowledgeable and we learned so much about the Louvre itself and the history of many of the pieces. The skip the line part was also amazing. Even in October there were many long lines and we got in right away. We were also directed to all the major highlights easily a A great experience. We loved it!

After an overnight flight from Chicago we took the Skip the Line Tour of the Louvre with Fabrizia as our guide. She was excellent, kept our attention in our exhausted state and made it a wonderful experience. Her dedication and love of the art shows.
John Edward did an amazing job taking us through the Louvre and providing stories and details. I would highly recommend

We kicked our tour off early as everyone had arrived early. The guide had great knowledge of the Louvre's history, which I found really interesting. Her knowledge of the artwork was quite amazing! The group was a good size. I was able to hang around at the end of the tour to see some of the collection that we didn't get time for in the tour. I would recommend this tour for people that are interested in both the art collection and history of the Louvre.
It was a pleasant experience and with a short group, with nice curiosities. Francesca helped us with any doubt we had about the history of the louvre 10/10 would recommend
I absolutely loved Laura our tour guide. If you want to see the Louvre ... book this tour and make sure you get Laura as your guide!

We were a big family group and all excited to see the biggest museum. The meeting point was precisely mentioned and easy to reach and we reached there on time . Our guide john was just too good with his work explaining every lil thing worth mentioning . We wanted the tour to last more than 3 hours . It's a must do when in Paris

Guide was 20 minutes late. Knew alot about a few things. Mildly entertaining. Ended our tour early. Presumably so as not to be late to his next tour. Hmmm... Anyways, we got in, skipping the line, although we had to stand and wait for our guide. Got around to the high points offered in the tour. Survived the derogatory commentary of our guide. We were then able to spend a few hours on our own enjoying the museum. So it got the job done.

Our tour guide seemed to talk till the last set of eyes glazed over
We could have seen so much more
Also, we couldn't leave the meeting point right away due to the headset batteries being dead in a few people's units. This should have been checked by the tour company before sending the units out into the hands of their employees and customers.

Enjoyed this walking tour at the Louvre Museum and the guide was extremely knowledgeable. It was a great way to see so many of the beautiful sites that this museum has to offer. The meeting site was easy to locate and it was nice not having to wait in a line to enter the museum. We were able to see Venus de Milo and Mona Lisa, and so much more.

Anna was our tour guide and she was amazing! She was very well-informed and kept us all interested by testing our knowledge of the Louvre and it's history. It was so informative, interesting, beautiful, historic and absolutely mind-blowing!

We were very happy with Anna and our tour of the Louvre.

If I'd known that the Louvre was once the palace of the Kings I wouldn't have been put off by the idea of a day's visit to a museum.
John Edward, from York, was a fantastic guide. Very informative and he guided 25 of us around effortlessly. His stories brought the exhibits and the artists to life.
The Louvre was stunning. Architecture to make its nation proud and wonderful to see Louis XVI furniture on display also.
I didn't realise I would see the old castle walls and keep beneath the Museum which was another pleasant surprise.
I don't know why anyone wouldn't have a guided tour. You'd miss too much without one.

John E was our tour guide today.
Wow! He was so knowledgeable and this walking was fantastic. Thank you for showing us the Louvre today we enjoyed it so much.
Highly recommend this tour.
Thanks from Australia fans 🇳🇿

Our tour guide, Veronique (sp?), was great. She was very knowledgeable, friendly and gave us a great tour. We learned a lot of things we would have never noticed ourselves and made it very interesting. She was not afraid to tell us her own opinions on different works in the Museum which was great as well. We wanted to book the 1.5 hour tour as we thought the 3 hour would be a bit long which for us it was just a little, but we still enjoyed it very much. I would recommend adding more of the 1.5 hour tour options as I think they would be more popular for people who want to see just the main highlights. We only had 6 people in our group and 2 of them were secret reviewers for the company and left near the Mona Lisa so the tour was very personal which made it even better.

This tour was outstanding and truly the best way to see the Louvre museum. First, you truly do skip the line while being in a group accompanied by a guide--as opposed to just buying a "skip the line ticket" and standing in a 5-block, hour-long line as I did at the Musee d'Orsay the next day!
Our guide, John, was tremendous. Not only did he give us such interesting historical information, but he navigated us through the crowds so well(who knew, Monday is the busiest day!) so we never had a difficult time seeing the artwork or felt rushed.
I highly recommend City Wonders tours, ad if you there's any way you can get John as your guide, do so!

nice tour. host was pleasant and informative. would recommend.
Louvre was fantastic but impossible to absorb in 1 trip

Our guide knew her stuff. It was a great trip to the Louvre. Anna was wonderful. Also, visiting the museum in October is a lot less crowded than during Summer travel season. Just know that this three hour tour has little opportunity to sit. You will be on your feet for a while. It's worth it, but prepare to do a lot of walking.

So happy I booked this tour. Our tour guide Ruben introduced us to several pieces throughout the museum. We got through the line at the Mona Lisa in about 10 minutes. Rubens knowledge and stories brought the art to light. We were also able to see Napoleons quarters which I never even knew were there. It was informative and worth the 3 hours. Would highly recommend.

First, I never received an email nor was there any information on the ticket about where to meet. So when I’m waiting by the pyramid at 0930 with no one showing, I continue to wait until 0940 and call the company listed on the ticket. They immediately inform me it’s at the arch, which is only a short walk. However, I get over there at 0946 and my group already left. Thankfully, I was able to attend with another group (thank you Mary) and she made the tour great.

Our tour guide Alex was amazing!!! He was so knowledgeable. He also had a great sense of humor. This tour included skip the line but there was noone in line when we got there. The group line which we were in was about a ten minute wait.

V glad had signed up with Guide. Alex was informative and had good sense of humour. Also took pains to check we could hear him thru out tour. The Louvre is massive and it would have been overwhelming to visit by ourselves since we hadn’t the time to do much prior homework. Word of caution: must be reasonably fit as a lot of stairs. I have to use a crutch as recovering from knee surgery (6 mos ago). Managed well enough but 3 hours can be v tiring

Tour was good and guide seemed to be very well informed. However, the audio quality was poor and it was very difficult to hear anything. The value of the tour was in skipping the line and being guided to the important pieces in the museum. Unfortunately the the audio quality diminished the overall experience.
Saved a ton of time getting through entrance and Mona Lisa. Knowledgeable guide. Saw a lot in 3 hours.

This tour was great! Our guide, Julia (pronounced in the Russian way, You-lee-uh) was incredibly knowledgeable about everything we saw and brought an interesting personal take to the works she showed us. We definitely saw the highlights: Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, Winged Victory, some other Leonardo work, and others from more recent French history as well as other Greek and Roman statues.

- Slight negative: as the tour name suggests, we did get to skip part of the line to get into the museum proper, but no one skips the Mona Lisa line, which was verrry long. However, Julia was well prepared for this, and showered our group with Mona Lisa history and details for almost the entire wait.
- The museum is VERY LOUD and thankfully there was a small mike/earbud system that let us hear Julia even in dense crowds, or when not standing right near her.
- The Louvre is simply mind-blowing and everyone should spend some time there when in Paris.

We absolutely loved this tour. Our guide was wonderful and took us to every highlight I wanted to see at the Lourve. We not only saw Mona Lisa but also 3 other DaVinci paintings. Her choice of other paintings was masterful. It would’ve taken us so long to navigate the Lourve for ourselves. We did all the best highlights in 3 hours.
Fab was great! She has great passion for her tours and love of art! We loved all that we saw along with her thorough narrative.
I enjoyed the tour and the guide’s commentary. Worth the time and money compared to going on your own.
Our tour guide Manny was awesome! Very informative and knowledgeable plus a little humor to keep it interesting. Skip the line is the only way to go!

What I liked about this is that we missed our scheduled tour, and the company accommodates is by letting us come the next day. Also, our tour guide Muhammad was pleasant and knowledgeable.

I will say this, there were hardly any lines so paying to “skip” the lines was unnecessary. Maybe it was because it was a Sunday and there wasn’t much people. But if I’d had known I would have just gotten general admission. Stood in line for almost 30 minutes to see Mona Lisa and only had ten seconds to take pics with/of it.

Ruben was our guide and he was fantastic. He kept us moving at a good pace and was very informative with all the pieces of art we viewed. Our tour unfortunately started later then scheduled because someone pulled the fire alarm just before we entered the museum which kept us locked out for an extra 30 minutes, so Ruben went out of his way to make up the lost time by showing us a few extra exhibits that went over his scheduled tour time. Great experience, highly recommended!

There were 26 people in our tour group. Way too many for a tour like this. I had understood that there would be 10 to 12 at most. The tour guide treated us like children and even used that tone. We were rushed thru the museum—I mean almost running from room to room through the royal rooms, royal jewels, etc and only slowed down when we got to the DaVinci paintings.
